name: disambiguate
why: Included by every tool that ACCEPTS the `qualified` argument (gh#37). Before it, a
`candidates` list was advisory: `Candidate` documented its `file` field as "the
disambiguating hint a consumer passes back" and no accessor accepted one, so a model
that read the list correctly and picked the identity it wanted had no move available.
Measured on this repo's own self-index: eleven memberdef rows are named `harvest` and
ten `reimplements` rows name `Harvester.harvest` as their base, so a bare call resolved
to a SUBCLASS and reported `overridden_by: []` — a confident empty answer about the one
identity with ten implementors.
The text names the FIELD to copy rather than describing a format, because a model that
has to construct the string will construct a plausible wrong one — this repo's own
record is that `Harvester.harvest` and `_CallSiteHarvester.harvest` both look like
valid selectors and neither resolves unless it is the full identity the payload
published. Copy, do not compose. That clause must never be cut from the served text.
Cut 2026-08-11 for the fixed-prompt budget: the most-multiplied block in the surface,
so a sentence here costs three times its length on the wire.
ROUND 2, 2026-08-11. Cut to the copy-verbatim instruction alone. Moved here, each
being a case where the argument is merely not useful rather than one where a model
would act wrongly:
* it selects an IDENTITY, not a signature — run(int) and run(double) share one;
* omitting it on a unique name is a no-op;
* an unmatched value returns the ordinary not-found envelope, which says so at the
time, and never widens the answer;
* `edge_class='key'` rows stay scoped to the BARE name;
* chain_trace does not accept it, and refuses an unknown argument.
text: `qualified` picks WHICH same-named function you mean: a `candidates[i].qualified` string COPIED VERBATIM from an earlier reply, never composed, with the name left BARE.
